brief: hooks/read-cap.sh caps certain tool calls per user turn in orchestrator mode. WebFetch is currently in its matcher and counted as a repository read. Stop counting WebFetch: a WebFetch call returns a small model's summary of a page, not a file's raw contents, so it should no longer consume the read cap or be refused by it. Keep read-cap's existing classification and cap behaviour for Read, Grep, Glob and Bash reads unchanged; only WebFetch's treatment changes. hooks/hooks.json also lists which tool_name values the PreToolUse matcher fires on for this hook, so check whether WebFetch still needs to be listed there once it is no longer capped. Run `bash tests/read-cap.test.sh`, which already covers the other capped tool types and will gain WebFetch coverage.

skills/visual/critique.py calls a vision-model critic to judge a generated image against its prompt. In a live run the critic scored the same unchanged image severity 2 on one call and severity 3 on a later call, which flips the local pass/fail rule (severity >= 3 fails). Make the critic's scoring deterministic across repeated calls on the same image: pin the request's sampling to the most deterministic setting the chat completions API offers. Only the critic call is affected; the image generation call in generate.py is unrelated and must stay as it is. Run `bash tests/critique.test.sh`, which stands in an OpenRouter server and will gain an assertion on the critic request's payload.

hooks/terse-governor.sh is a Stop hook that blocks replies over a word budget unless the reply matches a waiver regex for requests that legitimately need a long answer (things like a review or a list). A request asking for a recommendation, a summary, a comparison, an options rundown, or phrased as "what should ..." is currently still capped even though it needs room to answer properly. Extend the waiver regex to also waive the budget for these request shapes, matched as whole words only (so a word like "listen" or "playlist" containing "list" must not accidentally match and waive the cap). Run `bash tests/terse-governor.test.sh`, which already tests the existing waiver words and will gain cases for the new ones.

hooks/review-gate.sh unlocks the next builder dispatch or a git commit only after it sees a `git diff` run in the transcript. Its detection currently matches only the literal two words `git diff` with nothing in between, so a call like `git -C /repo diff --stat` after a builder step does not count and leaves the gate stuck refusing. Broaden the diff detection so a `git diff` preceded by git's own global options still counts: `-C <path>` and `-c <key>=<value>` (bare or quoted value), `--no-pager`, `-p`/`--paginate`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, and `--no-optional-locks`, in any combination before `diff`. `git log`, `git -C <path> log` and `git difftool` must still not count as a diff. Run `bash tests/review-gate.test.sh`, which already covers the gate's other refusal/allow behaviour and will gain cases for global-option diffs.

hooks/read-cap.sh treats a `jq` Bash call as a read whenever it sees two non-flag words (filter plus a file operand), to catch `jq . data.json`. This over-counts: a filter built with `jq -n --arg NAME VALUE` or `--argjson NAME VALUE` has two non-flag words but reads nothing, so it gets refused as a read for no reason. Judge jq calls by jq's own option grammar instead: `--arg`/`--argjson` each consume the following two words (name and value, neither is a file); `--indent`/`-L` consume their one value; `--args` and `--jsonargs` mean every word after them is a positional argument, not a file, so file-counting stops there; `--slurpfile`, `--rawfile` and `-f` still mark their following word as a file, counting as a read. Run `bash tests/read-cap.test.sh`, which already covers jq's basic file-vs-flag cases (issue #699) and will gain assertions for these option shapes.

Orchestrator mode has parallel builder subagents sharing one working tree (hooks/orchestrator-guard.sh already refuses large edits and unsafe Bash for the main session). A builder subagent ran `git checkout -- <path>` over files another builder had just finished, wiping that work, because subagent Bash otherwise passes through the guard untouched. Add one more check that applies specifically to a subagent's Bash (not the main session's, which already has its own broader allowlist): refuse, in orchestrator mode only, `git checkout` with a pathspec (`-- <path>` or `<rev> -- <path>` or a bare `git checkout .`), `git restore`, `git reset --hard`/`--merge`/`--keep`, `git stash` beyond `list`/`show`, and `git clean`. `git status`, `git diff`, `git stash list`/`show`, `git log`, and a branch-creating `git checkout -b` must stay allowed for a subagent. Gate the new check behind an env var that can disable it, matching the pattern other hook features here use for an opt-out. Run `bash tests/orchestrator-guard.test.sh`.

Two related fixes in the orchestrator hooks. First, agent dispatches now run in the background, so when hooks/review-gate.sh looks for a checker's FAIL verdict to sanction a retry without a full review, the checker's own tool_result in the transcript is only a launch stub — the real verdict arrives later as a `<task-notification>` entry (which can be a user or a queue-operation entry). Make the gate find that notification and match its tool-use-id back to the checker dispatch so it can still read the FAIL verdict from it. Second, wherever hooks/orchestrator-guard.sh and hooks/read-cap.sh print a refusal message, put the remedy (what to do instead) as the message's first line rather than after the explanation, so a truncated or skimmed message still shows the fix. Run `bash tests/read-cap.test.sh` and `bash tests/review-gate.test.sh`.

skills/visual/route.py is a UserPromptSubmit hook that reads the submitted prompt and, when it hits a word prefilter for an image/video/audio request, asks Jev to pick a model and adds guidance for Claude. A background-agent event (a `<task-notification>` or `<system-reminder>` block) also arrives through UserPromptSubmit as ordinary prompt text, and when its content happens to match the word prefilter, the hook fires again mid-task and calls Jev a second time, with Jev's pick sometimes drifting between the two calls. Make the hook silent whenever the prompt's stripped text starts with `<task-notification>` or `<system-reminder>` — including when there is leading whitespace before it, and even when such a block is itself wrapped inside another one — while a prompt that merely mentions those words somewhere in the middle of ordinary text must still route normally. Run `bash tests/visual-route.test.sh`, which stands in Jev and the catalogue.

hooks/orchestrator-guard.sh and hooks/read-cap.sh judge Bash commands segment by segment. Fix two gaps. False refusals: the shell keyword `continue` (and `break`, and the no-op `:`) as a segment's first word was refused as an unrecognised command though it reads/writes nothing — but must not launder a genuinely refused segment after it. `read` with an input redirect stays refused (dumps a file). Allow read-only git subcommands `check-ignore`, `check-attr`, `merge-base`, `for-each-ref`, `name-rev`. Allow branch creation only (`git switch -c`/`--create`, `git checkout -b`); a bare switch/checkout of an existing branch, a force-create (`-C`/`-B`/`--force-create`), `-f`, `--discard-changes`, `-m` stay refused. A write target still holding an unexpanded shell variable was already refused; give it its own message naming the unexpanded variable instead of the generic write message. Content-dump hole: `$(< file)`, its backtick form, and `x=$(< file)` expand to a whole file with no command word, so reader detection (which needs a command word) missed it. Close it: the guard refuses this shape, read-cap counts it as a read; `/dev/null`/`/dev/stdin` stay allowed. Run `bash tests/orchestrator-guard.test.sh` and `bash tests/read-cap.test.sh`.

hooks/orchestrator-guard.sh refuses a write-redirect target under the repo tree, but resolves a relative target only against the hook's own cwd. A command like `cd ~/.claude/projects/x/memory && echo - >> MEMORY.md` was wrongly refused because MEMORY.md was judged relative to the repo root instead of the directory the command actually `cd`s into. Track a preceding literal `cd`/`pushd` target within the same command and resolve later relative redirect targets against it instead of the hook's cwd — but only for as long as every operator since that `cd` is `&&` (a `cd` that fails after `;` or `||` would leave the shell in the original directory, so tracking must not carry across those; a `|`, a backgrounding `&`, a `!`, a skipped/untaken `cd`, and a `cd` that itself has a redirect must also reset the tracked directory). A `cd ..` must walk back up the tracked directory lexically, and a `cd` inside a nested command substitution must not leak into the outer command's tracking. This needs each segment's own separator and nesting depth exposed by the shared lexer in hooks/lib/tokenize.sh so the guard can decide when tracking resets. Run `bash tests/orchestrator-guard.test.sh`.

skills/visual/critique.py judges a generated image only against the generator prompt Claude wrote. A detail from the user's own message that the generator prompt dropped can never be flagged, since the critic never sees the user's wording. Add an optional user request to the critic pass: critique.py gets `--request`/`--request-file` (mutually exclusive) holding the user's verbatim message, sent to the critic as a second, clearly labelled section separate from the generator prompt (one section titled as the user's original request, verbatim; the other as the prompt sent to the generator); the critic judges prompt adherence against both, the request wins where they conflict, and request parts unrelated to the image are ignored. The request text must never reach the image generator itself, only the critic. generate.py gains the same two flags and forwards the request into its in-process critique.run() call after every raster/vector write. When critique.py builds an escalation retry (a stronger-model re-run after a failed pass), the request, when given, must carry into that retry the same way the prompt and defects already do. Without the flags, behaviour is unchanged. Run `bash tests/critique.test.sh`, `bash tests/generate.test.sh` and `bash tests/visual-route.test.sh`.
test_cmd: bash tests/critique.test.sh && bash tests/generate.test.sh && bash tests/visual-route.test.sh

brief: hooks/orchestrator-guard.sh and hooks/read-cap.sh each independently implement the same check for whether a git subcommand (plus its options and global flags such as `-C`/`-c`) dumps a file's contents rather than metadata — things like `show <rev>:<path>`, `cat-file`, `grep`, an unparsable global option, or a `-c alias.*` config, while `diff`/`log`/`status` etc. are not reads. Extract this into one shared function in hooks/lib/git-subcommand.sh, callable as `git_is_read` given the words after `git` (skipping global options), returning success/failure and setting a variable naming which case matched (for messages); both hooks call this shared function instead of keeping their own copy. read-cap.sh keeps exactly one case stricter than the shared one: an option after `show` that itself holds a colon (like `--format=%h:%s`) still counts as a read there. This is a pure refactor: no refusal/cap decision may change for any existing command shape. Run `bash tests/git-subcommand.test.sh`, which already covers subcommand parsing edge cases and will gain assertions calling the new shared function directly.
